matched.title: Guaranteed or unusually high returns with little or no risk
matched.why: Every investment carries risk, and higher returns come with more of it. A promise of big, steady or certain returns is the most common sign of fraud.

source.name: SEC Investor.gov, how to avoid fraud

matched.title: Pressure to act right away
matched.why: Fraudsters rush people so they don't stop to check. A real opportunity will still be there after you've looked into it.

source.name: SEC Investor.gov, how to avoid fraud

matched.title: An unexpected contact, or someone met online
matched.why: Many scams start with a message out of the blue, a wrong-number text, a dating app or a group chat, then build trust before any investing comes up.

matched.title: Paying in crypto, gift cards or a wire to a person
matched.why: Legitimate firms take payment into accounts in the firm's own name. Requests for crypto, gift cards or a wire to an individual are hard to reverse and common in fraud.

allSigns: Guaranteed or unusually high returns with little or no risk
An unexpected contact, or someone met online
Paying in crypto, gift cards or a wire to a person
Secrecy, inside information or an exclusive club
Someone posing as a firm, an official or a famous person
Asking for passwords, a recovery phrase or remote access
A hot tip that's about to take off
Fees or taxes to get your own money out
An offer to recover money you've already lost
No clear way it makes money, or it pays out from new members
